newsitem.title: USA: Gold prices slump to 20-month low.
newsitem.headline: Gold prices slump to 20-month low.

text.p: Gold prices fell to their lowest level in 20 months Thursday on selling by mining companies and U.S.-based investment funds.

Traders noted the market has been locked in a downward spiral since rallying to a high of $418.00 an ounce in February, hurt by a dearth of buying interest from investors who prefer to play in surging stock markets.
Some investment funds have even been building up speculative "short" positions in the market in anticipation that prices will fall further.

Weaker gold prices contributed to a fall of .51 point to 245.68 points in the Knight Ridder Commodity Research Bureau Index of 17 futures contracts despite a rebound in oil prices and another record high in natural gas.

"Gold is continuing to erode away in a very slow but steady fashion, with most bullion dealers looking for (a spot price of) $370" an ounce as a low before the year ends, Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.
Spot gold in the bullion market closed in New York quoted at $376.30/376.80 an ounce, compared with the New York close Wednesday of $378.20/378.80.
On New York's Commodity Exchange (COMEX), December gold futures closed down $2.50 an ounce at $376.50, just above an earlier new life-of-contract low of $375.80.

Crude oil, gasoline and heating oil futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange were boosted Thursday by forecasts of colder weather in the U.S. Northeast and ended higher across the board, recouping some of Wednesday's recent sharp losses.

After peaking in October, prices have generally been heading lower as worries about low heating oil stocks have waned. The latest Energy Department report showed that heating oil production by refiners continued at a brisk pace and inventories were recovering in the key Northeast market.
But a long sustained period of cold weather might again put the squeeze on prices, traders said.
NYMEX January crude oil rose 51 cents to $23.84 a barrel, December heating oil ended up 1.76 cents at 73.85 cents and December gasoline 1.65 cents higher at 67.04 cents a gallon.
NYMEX natural gas futures capped a six-day rally Thursday with a last-minute run to another all-time high before the December contract expired.

While a brief pullback was expected by some technicians who felt the market was overbought and due for a correction, most saw only limited downside with an Arctic air mass slated to blanket the United States next week.

On Thursday, December natural gas expired 27.4 cents higher at $3.901 per million British thermal units after earlier setting an all-time intraday high of $4.05. January, which takes the spot position Friday, settled up 4 cents at $3.304.
